summary: All fourteen findings confirmed; several fixes are corrected. /2 (high): item /24's Q̄_p^×-valued Proposition 2.19 is false (the CM counterexample over Q(i) holds step by step); the paper's Q_p^× version is right, and /25 inherits the error. /1: the paper is queued for design twice (DESIGN-BETTS-STIX #952 and the generated Part II job #3475), because make_queue only drops a generated job whose id matches a fixed one; the right fix folds the route into the fixed job, and the same bug duplicates DESIGN-BCGP18/25, DESIGN-SKINNER and DESIGN-PAN. /3: Σ_A are Q_p-points; E1's 'A reduced, hence étale' repair is false ('A split' is right), and Definition 6.8(c) should stay as printed. /4: the missing input is Shimizu's Theorem 7.4 (via Lemma 8.9), not Lemma 8.9 or Theorem 9.7. /5: Lemma A.2 is ambiguous rather than false in the reading its proof uses; the real gap is in the proof of Theorem 3.12(2). /7–/14 confirmed with small corrections (E6's instance proved prime by Pocklington; Remark 5.11 is an error, not a gap; /13 moves /28 to missing; /14's secondary point about 'without a model' is rejected).

sources.citation: arXiv:2204.13674v1 and its LaTeX source (the only arXiv version; the file the extraction read). The published Ann. of Math. text is not openly readable.
K. Shimizu, A p-adic monodromy theorem for de Rham local systems, arXiv:2003.10951v2, for finding 4.

findings.reason: I checked the generator, the queue, the git history and both issues. research/blueprint/make_queue.py puts every accepted part-ii route into `calls`. paper_designs groups these routes by the key ('part-ii', parent), and the job it builds is named DESIGN-<parent>PartII. The fixed list includes ('DESIGN-BETTS-STIX', 'GaloisSectionsPadicPeriodMaps', …, BETTS_STIX_BRIEF), and generated jobs are filtered against that list by job id only. The review accepted route 1 (parent AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty, roadmap GaloisSectionsPadicPeriodMaps). No other accepted extraction has a Part II route to that parent. So the queue holds both DESIGN-BETTS-STIX (order 7, roadmapIds [GaloisSectionsPadicPeriodMaps], after []) and DESIGN-AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabautyPartII (order 145, roadmapIds [AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabautyPartII], after []). Both are pending. The grouped job came in with commit 1018ef24, generated by the 7685a59f code. Issue #952 is DESIGN-BETTS-STIX, open and state:available; its body is BETTS_STIX_BRIEF and never names PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25. Issue #3475 is the grouped job, also open and state:available; it offers '1 continuation', 'Galois sections and p-adic period mappings … (48 items)', and points to the extraction. papers.json records the maintainer's routing as DESIGN-BETTS-STIX. The same paper is therefore queued for design twice, under two roadmap ids, and neither job waits for the other. That breaks section 15. The duplication will not fix itself either. The Part III check in paper_designs looks only for the id AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabautyPartII in the atlas, so the grouped job stays a Part II even after GaloisSectionsPadicPeriodMaps is designed. Two details of the finding are off, and neither changes the verdict. (i) The claim that 'the four source routes into MordellLawrenceVenkatesh import from GaloisSectionsPadicPeriodMaps by id' has no support: those routes never mention it, and only route 1, papers.json and the queue do. (ii) Route 1's reason already names DESIGN-BETTS-STIX, so that part of the fix is already done. Right fix: keep DESIGN-BETTS-STIX. In paper_designs, fold into the fixed job any part-ii or new route whose `roadmap` is the roadmap of a fixed design job, and add the route's proposal and a pointer to research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25.result.json (route 1's brief and items, and sourceIssues E1–E6) to DESIGN-BETTS-STIX's instructions. Do not simply drop the route. Also have the Part III check recognise an atlas roadmap whose recorded parent is the base, not only the literal id <base>PartII. Then retire #3475, since the job disappears from the queue.

The paper states Proposition 2.19 for χ: G_K → Q_p^× (reps.tex l.329, and the page image of p.13). Item /24 says Q̄_p^×, and with that change the statement is false. I checked the counterexample step by step. K = Q(i) is CM and is its own maximal CM subfield. For p ≡ 3 mod 4 the only place over p is v = (p), which conjugation fixes, so v is self-conjugate by Definition 2.17 and Remark 2.18(2). The curve E: y² = x³ − x has Δ = 64, so it has good reduction away from 2. The automorphism [i](x, y) = (−x, iy) is defined over K, so G_K commutes with Z[i]. V_pE is then a 1-dimensional vector space over K ⊗ Q_p = Q_{p²}, and G_K acts on it through a character ρ: G_K → Q_{p²}^×. Put χ = ι∘ρ. It is unramified away from 2p. At a prime 𝔮 ∤ 2p, ρ(Frob_𝔮) is the Frobenius endomorphism π_𝔮 ∈ Z[i], and π_𝔮·π̄_𝔮 = N𝔮, so every conjugate of χ(Frob_𝔮) has absolute value N𝔮^{1/2}. Hence χ is pure of odd weight. At v the reduction is good and supersingular (a_p = 0, so Frob_{p²} = −p), and the formal group is a height-1 formal Z_{p²}-module. So ρ|G_v is the Lubin–Tate character for the uniformiser −p. It is crystalline, and its Hodge–Tate weights are 1 and 0 at the two embeddings K_v → Q̄_p. Hypotheses (i) and (ii) therefore hold. But n is odd, and there is no single weight r_v, so 'n is even and r_v = n/2' fails under any reading. A small point: in the paper's conventions (geometric Frobenius; r with (C_p(r) ⊗ V)^{G_v} ≠ 0), V_pE itself has weight −1 and Hodge–Tate weights {0, −1}. Its dual, H¹, gives the finding's n = 1 and {0, 1}. Either way n is odd. I also re-checked that the paper's Q_p version is true. With Q_p values, η_p^alg is a product of local norms, so it is a Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p)-invariant character of the Serre torus. Pulling back along the isogeny N_{K/E} keeps it Galois-invariant, so its exponent a_τ depends only on the place of E that τ induces. Combined with a_τ + a_{τc} = m (a character of S_E, E CM), this gives r_v + r_{v'} = m, and the weight condition gives m = n. With Q̄_p values the exponent can differ between two embeddings that induce the same place, and the Lubin–Tate character does exactly that. When K has no CM subfield the Q̄_p version still holds, because every character of S_K is a power of the norm. So the error only matters when K has a CM subfield, which is the setting of Theorem 6.5. Item /25 inherits the error through 'under Proposition 2.19's hypotheses': here χ|G_v is Lubin–Tate, not a finite-order character times χ_cyc^{−n/2}, and n/2 is not even an integer. High severity is right, because the item is a false statement routed to the Part II design. The fix is right. For /25, make the item self-contained: 'for χ: G_K → Q_p^× as in Proposition 2.19'. The design of route 1 must plan the Q_p-valued statement.

I checked the following. locus.tex l.108 and p.45 define Σ_A := Spec(A)(Q_p), the Q_p-algebra maps A → Q_p, and V_ψ := Q_p ⊗_{A,ψ} V. Proposition 1.8 (p.5) has Σ = Hom_{Alg(Q_p)}(A, Q_p). Remark 6.6 uses Q_p-algebra maps. The definition of a symplectic pair (abelian-by-finite.tex) asks only for a finite-dimensional Q_p-algebra with continuous action, V locally free, and L free of rank 1. Item /78 says 'Σ_A the Q̄_p-points of A'. That is a different statement, with Q̄_p-coefficient V_ψ, which the paper neither states nor proves; its condition (b) (dimensions of D_dR of a Q̄_p-subspace) is not even defined in the paper. The étale clause in /78 is correct only for Q̄_p-points. The Q_{p²} counterexample is valid. Take K = Q, where every finite place is self-conjugate because Q has no CM subfield. Take A = Q_{p²} with trivial action, V = A ⊗_{Q_p} H¹_ét(E_Q̄, Q_p) free of rank 2 over A (d = 1), L = A(−1), and ω the A-linear extension of the Weil pairing, which is perfect. The pair is S-good: A is unramified, V is pure and integral of weight 1 outside S, and V is de Rham with Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1}. But Hom_{Q_p-alg}(Q_{p²}, Q_p) = ∅. So (a) and (b) fail vacuously, and (c) as printed asks 0 ≥ 2/2 = 1. Hence E1's second repair, 'A reduced (hence étale)', is false for the paper's Σ_A. The right hypothesis is 'A split'. The first repair, #Σ_A, is right, since with Σ = ∅ it reads 0 ≥ 0. E1's ε³ counterexample and its verdict are right: there Σ has one point of index 1, and 1 ≥ 3/2 fails. Every application has A|G_v ≅ H⁰_ét(X_{y_v,K̄_v}, Q_p) = ∏ Q_p, so A is split. The fixes to /78, /77 and E1 are right. Also replace the note on /78, 'Every use has A étale', with 'every use has A split'. One amendment: Definition 6.8(c) (item /79) needs no change. A definition cannot be false, and type (c) is only ever evaluated on H⁰_ét(X_{y_v,K̄_v}, Q_p), which is split, so dim_{Q_p}(A) = #Σ_A there. The containment of Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} in the union of the three loci still follows from the corrected Proposition 6.7, through the algebra isomorphism A|G_v ≅ H⁰. Keep /79 faithful to the paper; at most, add a note that for split A the two conditions agree.

The omission is real. The proof of Theorem 3.22 (p.31) begins: 'Since E has a full basis of horizontal sections, we have that E is potentially horizontal semistable [Shi20, Lemma 8.9]'. Its last step (p.32) uses B_dR(R_v)^{G_{R_v},∇=0} = K_v [Shi20, Proposition 4.9] to show that diagram (†) commutes up to GL_n(K_v). None of items /1–/100 states either fact. Item /48 only defines D^∇_pst and 'potentially horizontal semistable', with Corollary 4.10 and the dimension bound. Item /49 is Shimizu's Lemma 4.4 specialisation. Item /27 carries Shimizu's Theorem 9.7. Theorem 3.22, and through it Theorem 3.3 and §§4–7, therefore has an unplanned step. P8's description in data/atlas.json covers period sheaves, the Poincaré lemma and the proper-smooth comparison. R06.3 is the absolute monodromy theorem. No atlas stage plans a relative (horizontal) p-adic monodromy theorem, and nothing else mentions Shimizu. The citation in the fix is wrong, however. I read [Shi20] in the version the paper cites, arXiv:2003.10951v2 (named in its bibliography). The numbering checks out against every other citation in the paper: Definition 4.7, Proposition 4.9, Corollary 4.10, Lemma 4.12, Lemma 4.4 and Theorem 9.7 all match. In that version, Lemma 8.9 is only the dictionary: for an affinoid satisfying Brinon's set-up, D_dR of a local system is D_dR of the corresponding G_A-representation, compatibly with connection and filtration, and the local system is de Rham exactly when the representation is. The monodromy content is Theorem 7.4: if R satisfies Condition (BR), a horizontal de Rham representation of G_{R_K} becomes horizontal semistable over a finite extension L/K. Theorem 7.4 rests on Ohkubo's horizontal monodromy theorem (Shimizu's Theorem 7.1) and on the purity theorem of Shimizu §6. Lemma 8.9 does not rest on Theorem 9.7. Theorem 9.7 says that a flat bundle on a closed polydisc acquires a full basis of horizontal sections on a smaller polydisc. The paper uses it only in §3.1, where item /27 already cites it, and Theorem 3.22 assumes the full basis instead. Proposition 4.9 is stated as (B^∇_dR(R))^{G_{R_K}} = K, after Brinon Corollaire 5.3.7. This is the paper's statement, because the horizontal part of H⁰(Ū, OB_dR) is B^∇_dR(R_v). Right fix: add two items. (i) '[Shi20 v2, Theorem 7.4, via Lemma 8.9]: let R_v = O_v⟨t^{±1}⟩, which satisfies (BR). A de Rham Ẑ_p-local system on Sp(R_v[1/p]) whose flat bundle has a full basis of horizontal sections corresponds to a horizontal de Rham G_{R_v}-representation. That representation becomes horizontal semistable over some finite L_w/K_v, so it is potentially horizontal semistable: dim D^∇_pst(E) = rank E.' (ii) '[Shi20 v2, Proposition 4.9]: (B_dR(R_v))^{G_{R_v},∇=0} = K_v'. Optionally record a low sourceIssue: the paper cites Lemma 8.9 where the theorem needed is 7.4, and its 'Definition 4.15' for potentially horizontal semistable is Definition 5.6 in v2, where 4.15 is a lemma. The owner decision the finding asks for stands. A third candidate owner besides P8 or route 1 is DESIGN-PadicHodgeTheoryPartII, the pending Part II of PadicHodgeTheory. Its Guo–Reinecke proposal covers relative p-adic Hodge theory of local systems and already imports Shimizu inputs, and a relative monodromy theorem resting on Ohkubo and Brinon is p-adic Hodge theory, not Diophantine geometry.

I checked appx_derived.tex ll.25–29 (p.57) and the use at reps_in_families.tex l.339 (p.22). Lemma A.2 does not define 'bounded below', and it is the only use of the lemma. The counterexample is correct. The only nonzero E₁ term is E₁^{0,0} = gr⁰A⁰ = K, since gr^pA¹ = 0 for every p. All d_r land in zero groups, so the spectral sequence degenerates. But F^pA = [K → K] for p ≤ 0 and [0 → K] for p ≥ 1, so H¹(F¹A) = K → H¹(F⁰A) = 0 is not injective. The failure does not depend on the filtration being non-separated. For example, take A⁰ with basis y, u_1, u_2, … and A¹ with basis e_1, e_2, …, with d y = e_1 and d u_k = e_k − e_{k+1}, and filter by index (y in F^0, u_k and e_k in F^k). This filtration is exhaustive, separated and equal to everything for p ≤ 0. Every gr^p with p ≥ 1 is acyclic, so E₁ = E₁^{0,0} = K. Yet H¹(F¹A) = K and H¹(F⁰A) = 0. Two parts of the finding are overstated. In the other reading, F^pA^n = 0 for p ≫ 0 in each degree (Weibel's 'bounded below', translated to decreasing filtrations), the lemma is true and the printed proof is valid. The reduction to finite filtrations works by replacing A with F^pA, filtered by F^{max(k,p)}A: its spectral sequence still degenerates, and it contains the map H^j(F^{p+1}) → H^j(F^p) that has to be injective. So that reduction is neither superfluous nor wrong, and the lemma is ambiguous rather than false in the reading its proof uses. The substantive gap is real. The sentence on p.22 either applies A.2 to OB_dR ⊗_{O_U} Rπ_dR*E, whose filtration is bounded in neither direction and not complete (Fil^a OB_dR is never 0 and never all of OB_dR; see Remark 3.13), or applies it to Rπ_dR*E, which has a finite filtration and fits, and then passes silently to the tensor product. Either way, the claim that OB_dR ⊗ Rπ_dR*E has filtered cohomology objects, which the proof of Theorem 3.12(2) needs, is not justified. Medium severity is right. Right fix: add E7 as proposed (gap, affects the proof). Restate /99 with the hypothesis 'F^pA^n = 0 for p ≫ 0 in each degree'; this is true and covers the finite case, and a finite filtration is also acceptable. For the repair of Theorem 3.12(2), apply A.2 to Rπ_dR*E to get strictness. Then compute the cohomology of the tensor product as OB_dR ⊗ R^iπ_dR*E with the tensor filtration. That computation needs every quotient Fil^a/Fil^b OB_dR to be flat over O_U, not only OB_dR, together with the local freeness of the graded pieces of R^iπ_dR*E from 3.12(1). The fixer should cite Scholze for that flatness or record it as the missing ingredient, not assert it. The E₁-degeneration item is right. The proof opens with 'essentially contained in [Sch13, Theorem 8.8]', so this is a missing citation more than a missing argument; cite it as the finding says.

I checked (5.1) and the following text (big_monodromy.tex; the page image of p.41), the definition of the complex period map in §5.1, Definition 3.1, and Remark 5.7. All three define the period map by pulling the filtration back along parallel transport. The columns of T are horizontal: ∇(Te) = (dT)e + ωTe = 0. So T^∇ sends a constant vector e to Te, as the paper says. The pullback of F^i = span(e_1, …, e_{m_i}) is T⁻¹(F^i), the span of the first m_i columns of T⁻¹. The span of T_1, …, T_{m_i} is the push-forward. A concrete case: on A¹ take ω = [[0,0],[−dt,0]], which is flat, so T = [[1,0],[t,1]]. For F¹ = ⟨e_1⟩ the paper gives (1 : t), and the correct value is (1 : −t). S = T⁻¹ solves dS = Sω with S(0) = I. It has coefficients in K_v⟨t⟩, because it is the inverse of the isomorphism T^∇. On the complex side it is holomorphic, and ι(T⁻¹) = ι(T)⁻¹. So Lemmas 5.5 and 5.6, Proposition 5.3 and Remark 5.7 hold verbatim with T⁻¹, and 'affects: nothing' is right. I also confirmed the misprint in the proof of Lemma 5.6, 'Z_∞ ⊆ P^N_{K_v}' for P^N_C. The fix (E8 and item /67) is right. Record the P^N_C slip too, as a misprint inside E8 or as its own entry, since the fix as written leaves it out. Low severity is right.

Confirmed. I read Remark 6.23(I) in the TeX (locus.tex, p.54 of arXiv v1) and E6. The Remark takes r_0 >= 100 prime, larger than every odd prime dividing [K':Q], and q the least prime with q = 3 mod 4 and q = 2 mod every odd prime below r_0, and asserts that K' is linearly disjoint from Q(zeta_{q-1}). I redid the arithmetic without the red team's code. For r_0 = 101 the congruences define one class modulo M = 4*3*5*...*97 (about 4.6e36); its least positive member is 3458351945918277637129653220997634107, and that number is itself prime, so it is the q of the Remark (no smaller prime lies in the class). The finding calls q only a strong probable prime; it is in fact provably prime: q - 1 = 2 * 2423 * 2749 * 142475239163 * 1822097631939243653, each factor is prime (deterministic Miller-Rabin, all below 3.3e24), and 2 satisfies 2^(q-1) = 1 mod q and gcd(2^((q-1)/f) - 1, q) = 1 for each prime factor f, so q is prime by Pocklington's criterion (2 is a primitive root). 2749 is prime, 2749 = 1 mod 4 and 2749 = 1 mod 3. Hence Q(sqrt 2749) and the cyclic cubic subfield of Q(zeta_2749) both lie in Q(zeta_2749), which lies in Q(zeta_{q-1}). Both fields are Galois (K' = K), totally real so with no CM subfield, and 101 exceeds every odd prime dividing 2 or 3. So the Remark's hypotheses hold and its linear-disjointness claim fails; the cubic case shows the failure does not need [K':Q] even, so E6's reason ('if [K':Q] is even') is too narrow. (The other prime 2423 is 3 mod 4 and 2 mod 3, so it only yields the CM field Q(sqrt -2423); 2749 is the right choice.) E6's correction (take r_0 above every prime ramified in K') is right: Q(zeta_{q-1}) = Q(zeta_{(q-1)/2}) with (q-1)/2 odd is ramified only at primes >= r_0, so the intersection is unramified everywhere and equals Q. 'affects: nothing' stands, since Remark (I) is used by nothing and its conclusion holds after the correction. One wording change to the fix: 'can be nontrivial whenever such a prime ramifies in K'' overstates it (ramification of such an r in K' is necessary for a nontrivial intersection, not sufficient: the ramification may not come from an abelian subfield). Write instead: K' cap Q(zeta_{q-1}) = K' cap Q(zeta_{(q-1)/2}) is an abelian field ramified only at primes r >= r_0 dividing q - 1; it is Q when no such prime ramifies in K', and otherwise it can be nontrivial of odd or even degree, as the explicit instance shows (r_0 = 101, q as above, K = Q(sqrt 2749) or the cubic subfield of Q(zeta_2749)). Record q as proven prime rather than as a probable prime.

Confirmed, all seven, with two corrections to the fix. None of them is among E1-E6 or mentioned in the review. (1) Remark 5.11 (p.43) inherits from Corollary 5.10 only 'Y a smooth curve over K_v' and then covers Y(K_v) by finitely many discs 'by compactness', which needs Y proper. The counterexample is right: the Legendre family over Y = P^1 minus {0,1,infinity} over Q_p is an abelian-by-finite family (Y' = Y) whose monodromy Gamma(2) is Zariski-dense in SL_2 = Sp_2, so it has full monodromy. Any closed disc in Y^an is an affinoid, on which the coordinate t is bounded, so it contains only finitely many points of C = {p^(-n) : n >= 1}; a finite image is not Zariski-dense in the period domain, which here is P^1. So the Remark's hypothesis holds for every y_0 and every disc, yet C is infinite. Section 6 fixes Y a smooth projective curve, so every use (the Remark and the 'by compactness' in the proof of Corollary 6.11) is fine. Because the Remark's claim is false as stated, not merely unproved, record it with kind 'error' and affects 'nothing' rather than 'gap'. In item /70 add 'Y proper' only to the Remark 5.11 clause; Corollary 5.10 itself is right for any smooth curve. (2) Lemma 4.7 (p.35) assumes only pi smooth but uses the identification H^2_dR(X/Y)_y = H^2_dR(X_y/L), a base-change isomorphism that holds for smooth proper pi but not for smooth pi in general. The finding's example is correct (A^2 minus the origin over A^1 by x: the fibres have H^1_dR equal to 0 for x != 0 and K at x = 0, and the relative H^1 is 0), but it is in degree 1. A degree-2 instance is X = (A^2 minus the origin) x G_m over A^1 by x: for x != 0 the fibre A^1 x G_m has H^2_dR = 0, at x = 0 the fibre G_m x G_m has H^2_dR = K, while the relative H^2 is the x-power-torsion module K[x,1/x]/K[x], whose fibre at 0 is zero. The construction and the fibre compatibility survive for any smooth pi if 'identify' is read as the base-change map, so this is a gap in the statement, affecting nothing: every use is for an abelian scheme over a finite etale cover, which is proper. Adding 'pi proper' to item /57 is right. (3) p.36 (abelian-by-finite.tex, the definition of c_1(lambda)_{/Y}): 'the Poincare line bundle on X x_{Y'} X'; pp.33-34 have X x_{Y'} X^dual, which is what (1,lambda)^*P needs. A misprint. (4) (4.3), p.38: the product is indexed by y'_0 in |Y'_{y_0}| while its factors are Res^{L_{w_i}}_{K_v} H_{y'_i}. A misprint; item /62 already writes the product over i, so it needs no change, and folding this into E4 is reasonable. (5) p.29: 'Now we turn to the proof of Theorem 3.3 ... The first step is to reduce to the case of spherical polyannuli' comes right after the proof of Theorem 3.3 from Theorem 3.22 is finished, and the next result, Lemma 3.23, is the reduction of Theorem 3.22. It should read Theorem 3.22. A misprint. (6) p.50, proof of Lemma 6.17: in Phi'_ij = (sigma_j tensor phi^{m_j})(Phi'_i1) the index i is fixed and j runs over the r embeddings, so 'for all i' should be 'for all j'. A misprint; item /86 does not copy it. (7) p.54, Remark 6.23(I): 'where r runs over odd prime factors of q' should be 'of q - 1', as the product sign over r | q - 1 shows (q is prime). A misprint. E9-E15 numbering assumes findings /5 and /6 take E7 and E8; the fixer should number whatever is free.

Confirmed. (a) Remark 6.23 condition (2) (p.53) reads 'q - 1 is not divisible by 4 or any odd prime divisor of q_v * prod_{i=1}^{3}(q_v^i - 1)'. Item /93 writes 'q - 1 is prime to 4', which means gcd(q - 1, 4) = 1, i.e. q - 1 odd. That never holds for an odd prime q, so the item's condition (2) is unsatisfiable. (b) Part (III) (p.54) says the least q for (1)-(3) is 11 'with the modification of (3) for places of good reduction', meaning n_v replaced by 2. Item /93 keeps 'n_v replaceable by 2 at good reduction' in its statement of (3) but drops the qualifier from (III). I recomputed with g = 3 and zeta(6) = pi^6/945 = 1.01734: at q = 11 the right side of (3) is 1/(2.5*10 + 1) = 1/26 = 0.0385; with n_v = 7 the left side is 7*zeta(6)*8/1000 = 0.0570, so (3) fails, and with n_v = 2 it is 0.0163, so (3) holds. n_v, the number of extensions of K_v of degree 2 or 3 in an algebraic closure, is 7 for v not dividing 6 and at least 7 when v divides 6, so without the modification q = 11 fails at every place. The qualifier carries the whole comparison in (III). Condition (2) always excludes q - 1 divisible by 4 or by 3 (3 always divides q_v(q_v - 1)(q_v + 1)). With the unmodified (3), q = 3 and 7 are excluded, q = 11 fails (3), and q = 19 fails (2), so the least q would be 23, the same as for 1°-4°. At q = 23 with n_v = 7 the left side is 0.0054 < 1/56 = 0.0179, and (2) can be met with q_v of order 5 or 10 mod 11. The paper's values 23 (for 1°-4°, since q - 1 must avoid 3, 5 and 7) and 11 (modified) check out. The fix is right: '(2) q - 1 is not divisible by 4 or by any odd prime dividing q_v prod_{i<=3}(q_v^i - 1)', and '11 for (1)-(3) with n_v replaced by 2 (places of good reduction)'. It would help to add that without the modification the least q is 23.

Confirmed; each checked against the TeX and the page images. /32, Proposition 3.5 (p.17): the paper assumes pi: X -> Y a smooth proper morphism of smooth K_v-varieties, y_0 in Y(K_v), and U_{y_0} an admissible open neighbourhood isomorphic to a closed polydisc over which H^i_dR(X/Y)^an has a full basis of horizontal sections. The item states none of these, whereas the neighbouring item /31 (Theorem 3.3) does. /44, Proposition 3.19 (p.27): each part assumes smooth proper varieties (X/L_w in (1); X/L_{w_1} in (3); X, Y/L_w in (4); and naturality in (2) is among them). The item states none. Since c_dR of (3.8) is defined only for smooth proper X (item /43), the dropped hypothesis is implicit, so this is presentation only, but the protocol asks for every hypothesis. /45, Proposition 3.20 (pp.27-28): (5) and (6) assume X/L_w smooth proper and geometrically connected of dimension n (the item's H^{2n} and a^{tensor n} use this undefined n), and (7) and (8) assume X/L_w smooth proper. The item drops all of these.
